title: Funeral jobs during the Depression and low pay
summary: They talk about who played with Allen and the few dollars a funeral or night paid in the Depression.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Yeah, hold on. Do you remember some of the old fellas was playing with Old Man Allen when you played the funeral or whatever? Was Eddie Jackson playing with him? No. You don't remember that.
Uh-uh. I'm going to tell you the facts. I can't call back that for a man. The guy that's playing in the parade there.
Uh, about how long ago was that? When was that about? How old were you?
Was that during the Depression or? Dad was during the Depression. Back in those days. Yeah, that was during the Depression. You were playing Algiers?
Algiers. That would be a dollar and a half, huh?
Yeah, we made about two and a half. We were down and a half. Yeah, we were all over there.
All the way to Walker Town. Well, I think we made $4 that day.
Yeah. Now, quite as a kid, I haven't made 75 cents a night. Yeah. Playing music.
